agent.answer: El límite de contraparte para las SOFOM se reduce del 20% al 15% del capital neto según el artículo 5 de la Circular 12/2025 [REG-1].

The database does not contain information about the number of days credit institutions have to adjust their risk management systems to the new SOFOM counterparty limit. While it confirms the reduction of the SOFOM counterparty limit from 20% to 15% of net capital (cite_as: REG-1), no regulatory text specifies a deadline for implementation.

Therefore, the required adjustment period is not available in the database.  
**Recommendation**: Consult the full text of Circular 12/2025 — Modificación límites de apalancamiento SOFOM (cite_as: REG-1) or the CNBV official portal for the specific timeline.

The relevant regulation is:

- **Circular 15/2025 — Requisitos de reporte PLD/AML para instituciones fintech**, Article 3:  
  "Las ITF deberán designar un oficial de cumplimiento certificado en materia de PLD dentro de los ciento ochenta días naturales siguientes a la entrada en vigor de esta Circular."  
  [REG-1]

This means that ITFs must designate a certified compliance officer for PLD within **180 natural days** after the circular enters into force.

The circular entered into force on April 6, 2025 (the day after its publication on April 5, 2025).

Therefore, the deadline for designating the officer is **July 4, 2025** (180 days after April 6, 2025).

No cross-jurisdictional equivalent is required here, as the question is specific to CNBV (Mexico) and PLD.

**Final Answer:**  
ITFs must designate a certified compliance officer in PLD within **180 natural days** of the circular's entry into force, which is **July 4, 2025**.  
[cite_as: REG-1]

El nuevo coeficiente de capital neto mínimo para la banca múltiple es del **12%** del total de activos ponderados por riesgo, incrementado desde el **10.5%** anterior.

Este cambio se establece en la Circular 18/2025 del CNBV, publicada el 15 de abril de 2025 [REG-1]. No se encontró información sobre un equivalente previo en el SEC, por lo que no se puede confirmar si existe una correspondencia directa en Estados Unidos.  

**Acción recomendada:** Verificar si el contrato de banca múltiple incluye cláusulas que reflejen este cambio, especialmente en el cálculo de capital y riesgo. Se sugiere revisar el impacto en procesos de riesgo y capital.  

*Nota: El cambio es de alta relevancia para la estabilidad de capital y debe ser implementado en los sistemas de gestión de riesgos.*

No se establecieron límites específicos para invertir en criptoactivos dentro de las AFORES en la información disponible.

La búsqueda por "límites para invertir en criptoactivos en AFORES" en la CNBV no devolvió resultados relevantes. La única coincidencia encontrada es una modificación sobre el límite de contraparte para SOFOM (no relacionada con criptoactivos o AFORES), citada como [REG-1].

Se recomienda consultar la regulación oficial de la CNBV sobre inversiones en criptoactivos en AFORES o verificar si existe una circular específica sobre este tema, ya que actualmente no hay evidencia en el sistema de registros de dicha regulación.

Si se requiere, puedo ayudar a buscar si existe una equivalencia en la SEC (EE.UU.) o si hay alertas de impacto relacionadas.

The contract relevant to derivatives master agreements with SOFOMs is the **SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement** (Clause 3.1, Risk area).

Currently, the clause states:  
*"Credit exposure and leverage ratios shall comply with the capital adequacy requirements set forth by the CNBV and Basel III standards. The maximum leverage ratio is established at the regulatory threshold in force at the time of each calculation."*

**Context**:  
Circular 12/2025 (CNBV) introduces a new requirement for derivatives master agreements with SOFOMs to include an automatic adjustment clause when exposure exceeds the threshold set in Article 5. However, the current contract clause does not explicitly reference leverage limits or automatic adjustment mechanisms.  

**Action needed**:  
The contract clause does not currently align with the new CNBV requirement. A review and update of Clause 3.1 to incorporate an automatic exposure adjustment mechanism is required.  

*Note: No equivalent SEC regulation has been identified for this CNBV change (cross-jurisdiction mapping not available).*

**ADDENDUM TO ISDA DERIVATIVE TRADING MASTER AGREEMENT**  
**Effective Date:** [DATE]  
**Parties:** [PARTY A] and [PARTY B]  

---

**RECITALS**  

WHEREAS, the International Swaps and Derivatives Association, Inc. (“ISDA”) has established the Derivative Trading Master Agreement (“Master Agreement”) as a standard contract for derivative transactions;  

WHEREAS, the Comisión Nacional de Valores y Bolsas (CNBV) issued **Circular 12/2025 — Modificación límites de apalancamiento SOFOM**, dated March 20, 2025, which contains Article 5, specifying a new limit on counterparty exposure for Societies of Financial Object Multiple (SOFOM);  

WHEREAS, Article -5 of said Circular establishes that: *“El límite de contraparte para operaciones de Sociedades Financieras de Objeto Múltiple (SOFOM) se reduce del veinte por ciento (20%) al quince por ciento (15%) del capital neto de la institución.”*;  

WHEREAS, the Master Agreement, as currently executed, does not contain a specific reference to the SOFOM counterparty exposure limit, nor does it incorporate the regulatory requirement set forth in CNBV Circular 12/2025, Article 5;  

NOW THEREFORE, in order to ensure compliance with the regulatory requirements imposed by CNBV Circular 12/2025, and to reflect the updated counterparty exposure limit for SOFOM entities, the parties agree as follows:  

---

**ARTICLE 1 — AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 6.1**  
Clause 6.1 of the ISDA Derivative Trading Master Agreement is hereby amended as follows:  

The current text of Clause 6.1:  
*“Swap, forward, and option transaction limits shall comply with the derivative exposure rules established by the applicable regulatory authority. Capital requirements for derivative positions follow Basel III standards.”*  

is amended to read:  
*“Swap, forward, and option transaction limits shall comply with the derivative exposure rules established by the applicable regulatory authority. Capital requirements for derivative positions shall follow Basel III standards, and for transactions involving a counterparty that is a Society of Financial Object Multiple (SOFOM), the maximum exposure limit shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the net capital of such SOFOM entity.”*  

---

**ARTICLE 2 — AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 8.2**  
Clause 8.2 of the ISDA Derivative Trading Master Agreement is hereby amended as follows:  

The current text of Clause 8.2:  
*“Leverage and capital adequacy requirements for derivative instruments shall be recalculated upon any regulatory amendment affecting counterparty credit risk, including changes mandated by Basel/Basilea framework updates.”*  

is amended to read:  
*“Leverage and capital adequacy requirements for derivative instruments shall be recalculated upon any regulatory amendment affecting counterparty credit risk, including changes mandated by Basel/Basilea framework updates, and specifically, upon any modification to the counterparty exposure limit for a SOFOM entity as set forth in CNBV Circular 12/2025, Article 5.”*  

---

**ARTICLE 3 — GENERAL PROVISIONS**  

All other provisions of the ISDA Derivative Trading Master Agreement remain in full force and effect, unless otherwise modified by this Addendum.  

This Addendum shall be governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which the Master Agreement was originally executed, or if such jurisdiction is not specified, by the laws of [JURISDICTION].  

This Addendum may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.  

---

**EXECUTION**  

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have caused this Addendum to be executed by their duly authorized representatives as of the date first written below.

Date: [DATE]  

[PARTY B]

Date: [DATE]

WHEREAS, [PARTY A] and [PARTY B] entered into the Master Investment Agreement — Fintech ABC (the “Agreement”) on [ORIGINAL SIGNING DATE], as amended from time to time;  

WHEREAS, the National Banking and Financial Commission of Mexico (CNBV) issued Circular 12/2025 — *Modificación límites de apalancamiento SOFOM* on March 20, 2025, which modifies the leverage limits applicable to Societies of Financial Object Multiple (SOFOM);  

WHEREAS, Article 5 of said Circular 12/2025 establishes a new regulatory requirement that the counterparty exposure limit for SOFOMs shall be reduced from twenty percent (20%) to fifteen percent (15%) of the institution’s net capital;  

WHEREAS, the current counterparty exposure limit in Clause 4.2 of the Agreement exceeds the regulatory threshold set forth in Article 5 of the Circular 12/2025;

---

**ARTICLE 1 — AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 4.2**  

Clause 4.2 of the Master Investment Agreement — Fintech ABC is hereby amended as follows:  

The counterparty exposure limit shall not exceed **fifteen percent (15%)** of the total portfolio value. Any modification to applicable leverage limits imposed by regulatory authorities shall trigger an automatic review of this clause.  

This amendment is effective immediately upon execution of this Addendum and shall apply to all future investments, portfolio allocations, and risk assessments under the Agreement.

This amendment shall be applied to all fund structures, sub-funds, and investment vehicles managed under the Agreement, and shall be incorporated into all internal risk governance and compliance protocols.  

---

**GENERAL PROVISIONS**  

All other provisions of the Master Investment Agreement — Fintech ABC remain in full force and effect, except as modified herein.  

This Addendum shall be governed by and interpreted in accordance with the laws of the Federal District of Mexico, Republic of Mexico.

addendum.draft:
**ADDENDUM TO SOFOM XYZ LOAN PORTFOLIO AGREEMENT**  
**Effective Date:** [DATE]  
**Parties:** [PARTY A] and [PARTY B]  

---

**RECITALS**  

WHEREAS, the National Banking Commission of Venezuela (CNBV) issued Circular 12/2025 — *Modificación límites de apalancamiento SOFOM* on March 20, 2025, which modifies the maximum allowed counterparty exposure for Societies of Financial Object Multiple (SOFOM);  

WHEREAS, Article 5 of said Circular establishes a new limit for counterparty exposure, specifying that the maximum counterparty exposure for SOFOM institutions shall be reduced from twenty percent (20%) to fifteen percent (15%) of the institution’s net capital;  

WHEREAS, the SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement (the “Agreement”) contains provisions relating to credit exposure and leverage ratios that must be updated to reflect the regulatory change set forth in Article 5 of Circular 12/2025;  

NOW THEREFORE, in order to ensure compliance with the latest regulatory requirements, the parties hereby agree to the following amendments to the Agreement, specifically in the area of risk management and capital exposure limits.

---

**ARTICLE 1 — AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 3.1**  
Clause 3.1 of the SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement is hereby amended as follows:  

The current text of Clause 3.1 is:  
*“Credit exposure and leverage ratios shall comply with the capital adequacy requirements set forth by the CNBV and Basel III standards. The maximum leverage ratio is established at the regulatory threshold in force at the time of each calculation.”*  

This clause is amended to read:  
*“Credit exposure and leverage ratios shall comply with the capital adequacy requirements set forth by the CNBV and Basel III standards. The maximum counterparty exposure for any single borrower or group of borrowers shall not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the net capital of the institution, as defined and regulated under Article 5 of Circular 12/2025 issued by the CNBV on March 20, 2025. The maximum leverage ratio is established at the regulatory threshold in force at the time of each calculation.”*  

This amendment is effective immediately upon execution of this Addendum and shall govern all future assessments of credit exposure within the Loan Portfolio.

---

**ARTICLE 2 — AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 5.4**  
Clause 5.4 of the SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement is hereby amended as follows:  

The current text of Clause 5.4 is:  
*“Capital requirements for the loan portfolio shall be maintained in accordance with Basel/Basilea III guidelines, including minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratios as mandated by the applicable regulatory authority.”*  

This clause is amended to read:  
*“Capital requirements for the loan portfolio shall be maintained in accordance with Basel III guidelines, including minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratios as mandated by the applicable regulatory authority, and shall further ensure that counterparty exposure does not exceed fifteen percent (15%) of the net capital of the institution, as specified in Article 5 of Circular 12/2025 issued by the CNBV on March 20, 2025.”*  

This amendment is effective immediately upon execution of this Addendum and shall govern all capital adequacy assessments and reporting obligations under the Agreement.

---

**ARTICLE 3 — REQUIRED SYSTEMS AND CALCULATIONS UPDATE**  
The parties hereby agree that the following actions shall be implemented without delay:  

1. The current numeric limit of twenty percent (20%) for counterparty exposure in all internal risk models, risk dashboards, and credit evaluation systems shall be replaced with fifteen percent (15%) of net capital.  
2. All downstream calculations, including exposure thresholds, stress testing parameters, and internal risk limits, shall be recalibrated to reflect the new regulatory cap.  
3. A formal validation report, signed by the Risk Management Officer and the Compliance Officer, shall be submitted to both parties within ten (10) business days of the effective date of this Addendum, confirming that all systems and processes are aligned with the updated exposure limit.  
4. Any deviation from the 15% threshold must be immediately reported to the Board of Directors and the CNBV, in accordance with the regulatory requirements of Circular 12/2025.  

This update is classified as **HIGH PRIORITY** and shall be treated as a material change to the Agreement’s risk framework.

---

**GENERAL PROVISIONS**  

All other provisions of the SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement remain in full force and effect, except as expressly modified herein.  

This Addendum shall be governed by the laws of the Republic of Venezuela, as applicable to financial institutions and capital adequacy regulations.  

This Addendum may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.  

---

**EXECUTION**  

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Addendum as of the date first written below.  

[PARTY A]  
By: ___________________________  
Name: [FULL NAME]  
Title: [TITLE]  
Date: [DATE]  

[PARTY B]  
By: ___________________________  
Name: [FULL NAME]  
Title: [TITLE]  
Date: [DATE]  

---  
*This Addendum is issued in response to CNBV Circular 12/2025, Article 5, dated March 20, 2025, and is intended to ensure full compliance with the revised counterparty exposure limits for SOFOM institutions.*

**ADDENDUM TO CLIENT ONBOARDING AND AML POLICY**  
**Effective Date:** [DATE]  
**Parties:** [PARTY A] and [PARTY B]  

---

**RECITALS**  

WHEREAS, the National Banking and Financial Supervision Commission (CNBV) issued Circular 15/2025 — *Requisitos de reporte PLD/AML para instituciones fintech* — on April 05, 2025, which establishes new requirements for anti-money laundering (AML) and beneficial ownership reporting for Financial Technology Institutions (ITF);  

WHEREAS, Article 1 of said Circular 15/2,2025 introduces a new obligation requiring Financial Technology Institutions (ITF) subject to the Fintech Law to implement AML controls equivalent to those required of multiple banking institutions;  

WHEREAS, the Client Onboarding and AML Policy currently governs the institution’s compliance with AML and PLD obligations, including customer due diligence and suspicious activity reporting;  

WHEREAS, the regulatory change necessitates a formal amendment to ensure alignment with the new legal requirements;  

NOW THEREFORE, in order to comply with the provisions of Circular 15/2025, particularly Article 1, the parties hereby agree to the following modifications to the Client Onboarding and AML Policy:  

---

**ARTICLE 1 — AMENDMENT TO SECTION 2.1**  
Section 2.1 of the Client Onboarding and AML Policy is hereby amended as follows:  

The existing text of Section 2.1 is deleted and replaced with:  

> **Section 2.1: Customer due diligence (CDD) and enhanced due diligence (EDD) procedures must comply with anti-money laundering (AML) and PLD regulations, including FATF/GAFI recommendations and applicable national legislation.**  
> **In addition, all Financial Technology Institutions (ITF) subject to the Fintech Law shall implement anti-money laundering (AML) controls equivalent to those required of multiple banking institutions, as established under Article 1 of CNBV Circular 15/2025.**  

---

**ARTICLE 2 — AMENDMENT TO SECTION 4.3**  
Section 4.3 of the Client Onboarding and AML Policy is hereby amended as follows:  

The existing text of Section 4.3 is deleted and replaced with:  

> **Section 4.3: Suspicious activity reports (SAR) and regulatory disclosure obligations must be submitted within the timeframes established by the applicable AML/PLD regulatory framework. All reporting thresholds shall be updated upon regulatory amendment.**  
> **In addition, the institution shall ensure that its internal AML controls, including customer onboarding and risk assessment processes, are designed and maintained to meet the AML standards equivalent to those required of multiple banking institutions, as mandated by Article 1 of CNBV Circular 15/2025.**  

---

**ARTICLE 3 — GENERAL PROVISIONS**  
All other provisions of the Client Onboarding and AML Policy remain in full force and effect, unless otherwise modified by this Addendum.  

This Addendum shall be governed by the laws of [JURISDICTION], including all applicable regulations related to anti-money laundering and financial technology.  

This Addendum may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.  

---

**EXECUTION**

**ADDENDUM TO MASTER INVESTMENT AGREEMENT — FINTECH ABC**  
**Effective Date:** [DATE]  
**Parties:** [PARTY A] and [PARTY B]  

---

**RECITALS**  

WHEREAS, [PARTY A] and [PARTY B] entered into the Master Investment Agreement — Fintech ABC (the “Agreement”) on [ORIGINAL AGREEMENT DATE], as amended, and the Agreement governs the terms under which investments are made and managed by the parties;  

WHEREAS, the National Banking and Financial Supervision Commission of Mexico (CNBV) issued **Circular 15/2025 — Requisitos de reporte PLD/AML para instituciones fintech**, dated April 05, 2025, which introduces new requirements for Anti-Money Laundering (AML) controls for Financial Technology Institutions (ITF);  

WHEREAS, **Article 1** of Circular 15/2025, specifically, establishes that “Instituciones de Tecnología Financiera (ITF) sujetas a la Ley Fintech deberán implementar controles de antilavado de dinero (AML) equivalentes a los exigidos a la banca múltiple,” thereby imposing a new obligation on fintech entities to implement AML controls equivalent to those required of banking institutions;  

WHEREAS, the obligations under Article 1 of Circular 15/2025 directly impact the operational and compliance framework of the Agreement, particularly in relation to investment due diligence, reporting, and risk management;  

NOW THEREFORE, in order to ensure compliance with the regulatory requirements set forth in Circular 15/2025, and to reflect the new AML obligations imposed on fintech institutions, the parties hereby agree to the following amendments to the Master Investment Agreement — Fintech ABC:  

---

**ARTICLE 1 — AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 4.2**  
The following clause is hereby amended to incorporate the new AML compliance requirement:  

Clause 4.2 is amended as follows:

WHEREAS, the Parties agree that the Master Agreement must be amended to reflect the updated capital requirement set forth in the Circular;

---

**ADDENDUM TO SOFOM XYZ LOAN PORTFOLIO AGREEMENT**  
**Effective Date:** [DATE]  
**Parties:** [PARTY A] and [PARTY B]  

---

**RECITALS**  

WHEREAS, the Central Bank of Venezuela (CNBV) issued Circular 18/2025 — *Coeficiente de capital neto Basilea III para banca múltiple* — on April 15, 2025, which introduces a new regulatory requirement under Article 1, specifying an increased minimum net capital ratio for multiple banking institutions;  

WHEREAS, Article 1 of said Circular 18/2025, Section “limit_modification,” establishes that the minimum net capital ratio (CCN) for multiple banking institutions shall be increased from ten point five percent (10.5%) to twelve percent (12%) of total risk-weighted assets;  

WHEREAS, the SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement (the “Agreement”) currently contains provisions relating to capital adequacy and leverage ratios that are subject to such regulatory change;  

NOW THEREFORE, in order to ensure compliance with the updated regulatory requirements, and in accordance with the provisions of the CNBV Circular 18/2025, the parties hereby agree to the following modifications to the Agreement, specifically in the area of risk management and capital adequacy.  

---

**ARTICLE 1 — AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 3.1**  
Clause 3.1 of the SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement is hereby amended as follows:  

The current text of Clause 3.1:  
*“Credit exposure and leverage ratios shall comply with the capital adequacy requirements set forth by the CNBV and Basel III standards. The maximum leverage ratio is established at the regulatory threshold in force at the time of each calculation.”*  

is deleted and replaced with:  

**“Credit exposure and leverage ratios shall comply with the capital adequacy requirements set forth by the CNBV and Basel III standards. The minimum net capital ratio (CCN) shall be maintained at twelve percent (12%) of total risk-weighted assets, as established under Article 1 of CNBV Circular 18/2025 — Coeficiente de capital neto Basilea III para banca múltiple, effective April 15, 2025. This ratio shall be applied in all calculations of capital adequacy, including but not limited to credit exposure, risk-weighted assets, and leverage metrics.”**  

---

**ARTICLE 2 — AMENDMENT TO CLAUSE 5.4**  
Clause 5.4 of the SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement is hereby amended as follows:  

The current text of Clause 5.4:  
*“Capital requirements for the loan portfolio shall be maintained in accordance with Basel/Basilea III guidelines, including minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratios as mandated by the applicable regulatory authority.”*  

is deleted and replaced with:  

**“Capital requirements for the loan portfolio shall be maintained in accordance with Basel/Basilea III guidelines, including minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratios and a minimum net capital ratio (CCN) of twelve percent (12%) of total risk-weighted assets, as established under Article 1 of CNBV Circular 18/2025 — Coeficiente de capital neto Basilea III para banca múltiple, effective April 15, 2025. All capital adequacy calculations, including those related to loan portfolio risk, shall reflect this updated threshold.”**  

---

**ARTICLE 3 — REQUIRED UPDATE AND SYSTEM VERIFICATION**  
The parties hereby agree that the following actions shall be implemented immediately upon execution of this Addendum:  

1. The numerical threshold for the minimum net capital ratio in all internal risk models, financial reporting systems, and capital adequacy calculations shall be updated from ten point five percent (10.5%) to twelve percent (12%) of total risk-weighted assets.  
2. All downstream calculations, including but not limited to risk-weighted asset (RWA) determination, capital coverage ratios, and stress testing outputs, shall be recalibrated to reflect the new CCN requirement.  
3. A formal verification report, signed by the Chief Risk Officer and Chief Financial Officer of [PARTY A] and [PARTY B], shall be submitted within ten (10) business days of the effective date of this Addendum, confirming that all systems, processes, and documentation are aligned with the updated capital requirement.  
4. Any deviation from the updated CCN threshold shall be reported to the Board of Directors and the relevant regulatory authorities within twenty-four (24) hours of detection.  

---

**GENERAL PROVISIONS**  

All other provisions of the SOFOM XYZ Loan Portfolio Agreement remain in full force and effect, except as modified herein.  

This Addendum shall be governed by the laws of the Republic of Venezuela, without regard to conflict of laws principles.  

This Addendum may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.
